title: 200K-Token LLM Serving on a 24 GiB Laptop with Just-in-Time State Management
content:
Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence
  [Submitted on 15 Sep 2026]
    Title:JustFit: 200K-Token LLM Serving on a 24 GiB Laptop with Just-in-Time State Management
View PDF HTML (experimental)
            Abstract:Capable open-weight models make local coding and reasoning attractive, but their context and execution state strain laptop memory. We present JustFit, an MLX-based inference runtime that combines KVExec for compressed KV execution, PhaseSwap for component residency, and StateTrans for state-preserving serving transitions. These mechanisms fuse reconstruction and coordinate just-in-time materialization and release, independently of model-weight quantization. In full-execution capacity tests on a 24 GiB M4 Pro MacBook running Qwen3.8-27B MXFP4, three independent runs complete 196,608 input and 16,384 output tokens, increasing completed single-request context from the mlx-vlm baseline's 30,720 positions to 212,992 (6.93x); a separate two-request run retains 229,376 positions in aggregate. In separate performance tests, a 32K-input, 64-output probe reaches 19.11 tokens/s, and a repeated 32K+6K workload has a median peak process footprint of 16,374 MiB. The integrated runtime answers 29 of 30 AIME 2026 problems correctly, showing how compact state and lifetime-aware execution expand local serving capacity while supporting extended generated reasoning.

report.summary: JustFit, an MLX runtime with just-in-time state management, lets a 24 GiB MacBook serve over 200K-token contexts on a 27B model.
report.background: Local LLM inference on laptops has become practical thanks to open-weight models and 4-bit quantization, but long contexts remain the bottleneck. Model weights can fit in unified memory, yet the KV cache and execution state grow linearly with context length, quickly exhausting 24-32 GiB machines. Existing runtimes like mlx-vlm cap out far below the 100K+ contexts needed for repository-scale coding and extended reasoning. Prior fixes focused mainly on weight quantization or KV cache eviction, which trades quality for capacity. JustFit attacks the problem at the runtime level, treating KV state, model components, and serving transitions as schedulable resources rather than fixed allocations, aiming to raise usable context without retraining or model changes.
key_points: JustFit combines three mechanisms: KVExec for compressed KV execution, PhaseSwap for component residency, and StateTrans for state-preserving serving transitions. Together they fuse reconstruction with just-in-time materialization and release of runtime state, operating independently of model-weight quantization so the two techniques can be stacked.

In capacity tests on a 24 GiB M4 Pro MacBook with Qwen3.8-27B MXFP4, completed single-request context rose from the mlx-vlm baseline's 30,720 positions to 212,992 — a 6.93x gain. Three runs completed 196,608 input and 16,384 output tokens, and a two-request run retained 229,376 positions in aggregate.

Performance is usable but modest: a 32K-input, 64-output probe reached 19.11 tokens/s, while a repeated 32K+6K workload showed a median peak process footprint of 16,374 MiB. That leaves headroom on a 24 GiB machine but signals that long-context prefill and memory pressure remain real constraints.

Quality held up in the reported evaluation: the integrated runtime answered 29 of 30 AIME 2026 problems correctly, suggesting aggressive state compression and swapping do not necessarily collapse multi-step reasoning on hard math tasks.

The work shows that unified-memory laptops can act as long-context serving hosts, not just toy inference boxes. It also suggests runtime state management, rather than weight quantization alone, is the next lever for expanding local context capacity.
report.impact: For the AI industry, JustFit shifts long-context serving from datacenter GPUs toward consumer laptops, potentially weakening the assumption that 200K-token contexts require server-class hardware. For developers, it means local coding agents could ingest entire repositories, logs, or documents without API calls, improving privacy and cutting cost, though 19 tokens/s throughput limits interactive use and the near-16 GiB footprint leaves little room for other apps. For regular users, it points toward more capable offline assistants and private on-device reasoning. The bigger lesson is architectural: just-in-time state management may be adopted by MLX, llama.cpp, and vLLM-style runtimes, making context capacity a software scheduling problem as much as a memory hardware one.
report.tools: To follow up, watch Apple's MLX framework, mlx-lm and mlx-vlm for local inference, and MLX community ports. llama.cpp, Ollama, and LM Studio offer easier local serving, while KV-cache compression research such as KIVI, H2O, SnapKV, and Quest provides the conceptual basis for JustFit's KVExec. vLLM's PagedAttention is also relevant for state-management ideas. Since JustFit is a paper, check the authors' code release and arXiv page for implementation details.
